title: Automated Logistics Query Routing
business: Global logistics firms managing high-volume, multi-lingual shipping inquiries.
problem: Manual triage of customer emails leads to significant latency in routing specialized requests to regional support desks, increasing operational costs.
solution: Utilize Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct to parse incoming customer inquiries and generate structured JSON outputs that identify the intent and required destination department, enabling automated ticketing.
steps: Define a system prompt that specifies the required JSON schema for intent classification and department routing.
Configure the model to accept incoming emails as user messages while maintaining a consistent system message context.
Implement a post-processing layer to validate that the model output strictly adheres to the expected JSON format.
Integrate the validated JSON output with the existing CRM API to trigger automatic ticket assignment.
outcome: Reduced manual intervention in ticket routing and faster response times for complex international shipping queries.
limitation: The model may occasionally produce non-compliant JSON if the input is highly ambiguous; this is checked by implementing a schema validation step before API submission.
